editorial.headline: Re-Guarantee Brokerage: A Fully Open Activity With a Clear Bali Position
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 66226 covers advisory and brokerage work in re-guarantee provision and related claim settlement, acting for and on behalf of the guaranteed party.
editorial.body:
KBLI 66226 is a specialist intermediary activity: it covers providing advisory and/or brokerage services in the provision of re-guarantees, together with handling the settlement of related claims. The work is performed for and on behalf of the guaranteed party. Its centre of gravity is therefore representation and intermediation within a re-guarantee arrangement—not merely the administration of a claim, nor a general consulting label detached from that arrangement.

The code is available across every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the activity is not presented as one reserved for a single class of operator. A business registering under this code may do so at any of those scales, provided its actual work remains within the defined scope: advice or brokerage in providing re-guarantees, and the handling of their claim settlements on behalf of the guaranteed party.

Nationally, the position is direct. The activity is TERBUKA to PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In practical terms, the record permits full foreign ownership at the national level; there is no lower foreign-share cap stated for this activity. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For founders, the useful discipline is to keep that national position separate from the operating scope itself: foreign ownership may be fully open, but the registered activity must still be the defined advisory, brokerage, and claims-settlement work connected to re-guarantees.

Bali does not add a block here. The province’s standing moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA, island-wide and permanently. This activity is marked OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and at the Besar scale its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi; the record therefore states that it is not blocked by that moratorium. The Bali conclusion is unusually clean: a PMA registration is not prevented there by the stated moratorium, while the national foreign-ownership ceiling remains 100%.
